sources.entry: bdg (Browser Debugger CLI) by szymdzum - A CLI and Claude Code skill for UI debugging in Chrome using the DevTools Protocol, including DOM inspection, browser events, rendered styles, and detailed layout information.

summary.one_liner: A command-line browser debugger that keeps a Chrome session open in the background so an AI agent or developer can drive a live page and inspect its network, console, DOM, styles and layout one shell command at a time.
summary.what_it_does: bdg starts a persistent browser session and exposes commands for navigation, clicking, filling forms, waiting for elements, and emulating viewport, mobile and color-scheme settings. It reads back telemetry: network requests and headers (including Authorization), HAR export, cookies (including HttpOnly), console messages, and a live peek --follow mode. For inspection it reports element styles with the CSS cascade, layout and visibility, page-wide audits (contrast, overflow, layers, animations), stylesheet search, the accessibility tree, and event listeners. Any Chrome DevTools Protocol method can be called directly with bdg cdp, which also supports searching and describing methods. Output is compact and designed to pipe into jq, and --json and --help --json are available for agents.
use_cases: debug a web page's failing request or console error from the shell
let an AI coding agent drive and inspect a live browser
reuse a browser login's cookies or tokens in curl requests
check element layout, computed styles and CSS rule origins
audit page color contrast and accessibility tree
profile performance metrics or throttle CPU and network
run parallel named browser sessions for testing
stack: Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Chromium or Microsoft Edge)
notable: Persistent background browser session driven one command at a time, suited to agent loops
Raw CDP access with --search, --describe and a suggestion system for typos and unknown methods
Includes HttpOnly cookies and Authorization headers for reusing a logged-in session
Ships an agent skill via bdg install-skill for Claude Code and other agents
Can attach to an already-open browser profile without reloading tabs
caveats: Requires Node.js 22.12+ and a Chromium-based browser; Firefox and Safari are not supported
Native PowerShell and Git Bash are not supported; Windows works only via WSL
Benchmark comparison in README is from November 2025 and the author notes the compared MCP tool has since changed
keywords: inspect live page step by step
